text:
Andrew Copp is an Ann Arbor kid playing big minutes for his hometown-area team at a hard time. With Dylan Larkin suspended while he waits out a trade, Copp has been near 19 minutes a night, and Detroit has needed every one of them. Detroit Sports Nation is already asking what he'd be worth to a contender, which tells you where some people think the Wings' season is heading.

The production is modest: 10 points in 21 games, three goals, and a scoring rate just below our talent range for him. The harder number is five on five. Detroit gets 47% of the expected goals with him on the ice, four and a half points worse than without him, and his own chance rate is down from last season.

There's a useful player in here. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him moving the puck out of his own end cleanly 62% of the time, and in the 85th percentile for primary shot assists. Evolving-Hockey noted last season's results ran ahead of his chances, though, so a rebound isn't automatic. Watch his line's shot share. That's where his value shows first.
